title: A single particle can interfere with itself
body: Shine light through two narrow slits and a pattern of bright and dark stripes appears, the signature of overlapping waves; Thomas Young showed this in 1801. The quantum shock is that electrons, atoms and even big molecules do the same, as if each one travels through both slits as a wave and only lands at a single spot when detected. Richard Feynman called the experiment the heart of quantum mechanics.

steps.label: Fire electrons at two slits, one at a time
Each lands as a single dot
Thousands of dots build up stripes
As if each one went through both slits

slides.heading: Look, and it vanishes
slides.text: Measure which slit each particle goes through and the stripes disappear, leaving two plain bands. Getting “which-path” information destroys the interference.

slides.heading: Not just tiny things
slides.text: The effect has been shown with molecules made of about 2,000 atoms, with a mass around 25,000 times that of a hydrogen atom.

slides.question: What happens to the stripes if you measure which slit each particle goes through?
options: They vanish, leaving two plain bands
slides.explanation: Getting ‘which-path’ information destroys the interference: the striped pattern disappears and only two plain bands remain.
